text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000030's 99215 rate is far above expectation in every complexity group, but the few returned charts all support the billed level, and duplicate-text and late-note signals leave open whether those charts reflect the visits.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing persists after risk adjustment and appears in every complexity stratum, including low-complexity visits such as C0012768 (no chronic conditions, URI diagnosis only) and repeated single-diagnosis depression visits for one patient (C0012607, C0012615); a sicker panel alone would not readily explain that pattern. Against this, none of the documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level (examples include C0012626 and C0012769), which points toward a legitimately complex panel rather than upcoding. That support is ambiguous for three reasons: records cover only about a tenth of claims, a third of returned notes show duplicate text, and a few claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim. Together these are weak signs of cloned or inflated notes, not proof. First, a reviewer should obtain the audit trail and compare the duplicate-flagged notes side by side. Then they should request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims, such as C0012631, which is also flagged for a late note, to test whether high MDM is genuinely documented on simple visits."}
